text: Marrow Bay Transit said its new Isolde-class ferry, the *Lumen Tide*, will enter service on 14 May with capacity for 1,800 passengers and 210 vehicles. The company said the vessel completed sea trials last week, logging 36 hours at a top speed of 24 knots and fuel use 11% below plan. Chief executive Rina Voss called the ship “a step-change in corridor throughput” on the Nare Strait route, where peak summer demand has strained older ferries. The $286 million program was financed through a mix of municipal bonds and port authority support. For the sector, the launch underscores a push toward larger, lower-emission vessels as operators chase higher load factors and lower unit costs.
